hypotheses.justification: `hmoll` is a closed Prop, `ContinuousExtensionConvexMollificationOnInteriorClosedBallTheorem n`, and the library proves it with no extra assumptions. The proof is `ContinuousExtensionConvexMollificationOnInteriorClosedBallTheorem.proof` in Jensen/MainTheorems.lean, line 42. It builds the approximants as convolutions with the normed bumps `jensenMollifierBump n ((R-r)/2) _ m` and uses three lemmas: `exists_pos_forall_rOut_le_abs_normedBumpConvolution_sub_extension_le`, `contDiff_two_normedBumpConvolution_left` and `convexOn_normedBumpConvolution_of_convexOn_extension`. All three, and `jensenMollifierBump`, are in the same file, ConvexMollification.lean, at lines 320–712. None of them uses the theorem under review, and neither directory has a `sorry` or `axiom`. MainTheorems.lean even defines `SmoothConvexApproximationOnInteriorClosedBallTheorem.proof` (line 92) by applying this theorem to that proof. So the conclusion `SmoothConvexApproximationOnInteriorClosedBallTheorem n` holds unconditionally for every `n`, including `n = 0`. To prove it without `hmoll`, keep the same argument (extension to an intermediate radius, then restricting convexity to the smaller ball) and replace the call `hmoll g G x0 Rmid r ...` with the mollification proof inlined. That proof would have to be moved below the helper lemmas, which come after this theorem in the file. Nothing else in the statement mentions `hmoll`, so deleting it leaves the statement well-formed.
